title: Build the Mez Systems Product UI and Data Visualisation foundation
objective: Establish a code-first product interface grammar and accessible data language through one evidence-backed operational workspace before expanding into product-specific workflows.

included: shared application shell, contextual navigation, command/search and responsive recomposition
one operational ledger using repository-backed fixture data
accessible table, selection, filtering, sorting, density and disclosure behaviour
one truthful data visualisation with a complete text alternative
loading, empty, error, stale, partial and no-permission states
keyboard, visible focus, screen-reader and reduced-motion proof
a candidate contract, workbench, verifier, review record and Gate B assessment
excluded: inventing production product screens, metrics, users or customer data
building every final product workflow in the first round
changing canonical foundations, identity or existing component decisions
deferred advertising, social, email, deck, document, video, icon, print or environmental channel systems
consumer repository ingestion, publishing or deployment
using Figma as independent behaviour or production authority

acceptance: source contract and schema define authority, data truth, anatomy, states, density, accessibility and responsive behaviour
review distinguishes measured results, unmeasured claims, known gaps and human decisions
verifier checks the contract against the implementation rather than JSON alone
the review surface uses only repository-backed fixture facts
the operational ledger is the visual protagonist rather than a generic metric-card dashboard
responsive, state, keyboard, focus, screen-reader and data-alternative behaviour can be exercised in the browser

verification.passCondition: authority, data lineage, accessible table and visualisation alternatives, state coverage and implementation behaviours pass
real renders at 320, 375, 390, 768, 920, 1280 and 1440 preserve order, hierarchy and access without body overflow
keyboard, focus, spoken labels, table semantics and chart text alternative are proven in the running workbench
Olli accepts, revises or rejects the candidate after a Gate B design critique

humanGate.approvalQuestion: Does this operational ledger establish a distinctive, credible and usable Mez product-interface grammar worth expanding into the real product workflows?

stopConditions: the candidate requires invented production data or customer claims
the interface becomes a generic card-grid dashboard rather than one coherent workspace
responsive behaviour hides meaning or requires page-level horizontal scrolling
a chart has no complete text alternative
the work enters a consumer repository, publishes or deploys
notes: SEQ-PRODUCT-UI-FIRST-001 records Olli's priority change; deferred channel systems remain future work.
The first review fixture is the design-system control plane itself because its data can be verified locally. It is not presented as a production Mez product screen.
Real AI OS and other product workflows follow only after the shared grammar is accepted and source evidence is available.
Round 01 passed its bounded verifier, responsive and interaction proof and Gate B at 67/75.
Olli approved the operational-ledger foundation direction through H-UI-01-PRODUCT-UI-FOUNDATION on 28 July 2026. The approval creates no canonical or production authority.
